clue.text: Hey, this is what a conjuror must say quickly

definitions.text: Hey, this is what a conjuror must say
definitions.meaning: a stage magician's catchphrase when the trick is revealed is 'Hey ...!'
in music the tempo marking for very fast playing

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition completes the conjuror's catchphrase begun by 'Hey'; the second is the Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician's cry completes 'Hey ...', and the same Italian word is a musical direction meaning very fast.

clue.text: He who calls to order audio equipment

definitions.meaning: the presiding officer of the House of Commons calls members to order
a loudspeaker on a hi-fi system

explanation.definitionFit: The chair of the Commons bears this title, and a loudspeaker on a stereo has the same name.

clue.text: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid

definitions.text: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid

parts.words: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid
parts.note: a 'hand' here is the set of playing cards a player holds and lays down, not a human palm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' and 'laid' suggest touching or blessing; in card games a hand is laid down on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding table used for bridge or whist, where players put down their dealt cards.

clue.text: Twins for example capsized small car

indicators.note: in a down entry a capsized word is turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
the Mini is the classic small British car

explanation.surface: Twins have somehow overturned a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns EG into GE in this down clue, then MINI follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux, is named with the Latin word for them.

clue.text: Deeply planted a ground cereal

parts.note: something deeply planted is set a long way inside, 'far in'

explanation.surface: Something buried deep is a kind of milled grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Farina is a flour or meal milled from grain, often wheat, used for puddings and porridge.

clue.text: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up

definitions.text: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up

parts.words: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up
parts.note: a climber needing support to raise a leg looks for a secure place for the boot on the rock face

explanation.walkthrough: 'A leg up' usually means help or a boost; here it is literal, a climber lifting a leg to a secure resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure place on rock where a climber can rest a boot, figuratively any secure position.

clue.text: Sound room for secretion

indicators.note: placed first, this word tells the solver to listen for a word that is said like the next one

parts.note: taken as written; it is the word heard

explanation.surface: A soundproofed chamber suited to some bodily discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, a bodily secretion.

clue.text: White notes Brown scaling Russian mounts

indicators.note: climbing, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Urals are the mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: Someone surnamed Brown, carrying white notes, climbs Russian peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; it is the colour TAN, which 'scaling' turns to NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: On a piano the white keys sound notes that are neither sharp nor flat, called naturals in music.

clue.text: Watch the gossip

definitions.meaning: a timepiece that chimes the hours or quarters again when a button is pressed
someone who passes on what they have heard

explanation.definitionFit: A chiming pocket timepiece has this name, and so does a tattler who passes stories on.

clue.text: The best policy produces silvery leaves in the garden

definitions.meaning: the proverb says truthfulness is the best policy
Lunaria, a garden plant whose seed pods dry into silvery discs

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names truthfulness as the best policy, and Lunaria, a plant with silvery seed discs, shares the name.

clue.text: Like a lady stiffly corsetted, or could one say stayed?

indicators.note: asks whether the word could be said the same way as the one before, a cue to listen

parts.note: taken as written; stays were the stiff bones of a corset, so a corseted lady is stayed

explanation.surface: A tightly laced Victorian lady is described with a play on her corset stays.
explanation.walkthrough: Old corsets were stiffened with 'stays', so the lady is literally stayed; the homophone gives the word for sedate and prim.
explanation.definitionFit: A primly upright, sedate manner suits a stiffly corseted woman; staid means sober and respectable.

clue.text: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer

definitions.text: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer

parts.words: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer
parts.note: read 'dark' as the hours of darkness and 'horse' as a female horse; this one visits only sleepers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' suggests an unknown contender; split it as night plus mare, the bad dream that comes only to sleepers, not daydreamers.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream comes only in sleep, so it cannot trouble someone dreaming while awake.

clue.text: Glacial material found up in, and also at foot of precipice

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry's word is its end, so take the closing letters

explanation.surface: Frozen debris lies at the base of a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two routes: 'found up in' reads the letters upwards inside 'precipice', and 'at foot of' takes the final three letters of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaciers are made of frozen water, so the material is frozen water.

clue.text: Far too grand for a mince pie actor

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters of the following words are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An actor in a Christmas pantomime is too grandiose for a little mince pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince pie' looks like the festive pastry; 'mince' is the anagram signal working on PIE ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown, melodramatic behaviour is likened to opera, so operatic means extravagantly grand.

clue.text: Beautiful appeal very abbreviated in famous portrait artist

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the name of the painter

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely, court portrait painter to Charles II
O is the exclamation of appeal or address, as in 'O Lord'
v is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A pleading request, shortened, praises the beauty of a famous portrait painter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: O (an appeal, as in 'O Lord') and V go inside LELY, after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very pleasing to look at; lovely is a close synonym of beautiful.

clue.text: Eccentric member of society

definitions.meaning: a strange person, a queer character
a member of the ..., a British friendly society for mutual aid

explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows is a long-standing British friendly society, a mutual insurance club; each member carries the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange character is a peculiar chap, and a member of the friendly society called the Oddfellows takes the same name.

clue.text: Criminal who runs a bankrupt business

definitions.meaning: a fence, someone who handles stolen goods
an official appointed to manage an insolvent company

explanation.definitionFit: A fence for stolen property is called this, and so is the court-appointed official who manages an insolvent company.

clue.text: Tiny electronic bulb went first

definitions.meaning: a light-emitting diode, a small electronic lamp
guided from the front, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: A light-emitting diode is known by its initials, and the past tense of guiding from the front is spelt the same.

clue.text: Description of spirits, anaesthetic and ale concoction

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture of ingredients, so the letters of the beer are stirred up

explanation.surface: A drink mixing ale with an anaesthetic would surely raise spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests strong drink beside 'ale'; here it means ghosts. 'concoction' turns ALE into EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts and spirits are airy and insubstantial, and that light, otherworldly quality is what ethereal means.

clue.text: To sum up, it was just half way through the first millenium

parts.note: the first thousand years of the Christian era are dated AD
halfway through a thousand years is the year 500, D in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Summing up history, someone notes an event exactly midway through the first thousand years.
explanation.walkthrough: The midpoint of the first millennium is AD 500, written with the Roman numeral D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to combine them into a sum, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Black necklace and ear-rings for the old yuppies

parts.note: jet is a black gemstone, so jet-black
a matching group of jewellery is a set

explanation.surface: Rich young professionals of old wore black jewellery sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black necklace' suggests jet jewellery, but the pieces split: JET for black, SET for the matching jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: The fashionable rich who flew around the world in the 1960s were the earlier version of the yuppies.

clue.text: Passed bill on the theatre's bill board?

definitions.meaning: a bill passed by parliament becomes law, a statute
a turn listed on a theatre's playbill

explanation.definitionFit: A bill passed into law is a statute of this name, and each turn listed on a theatre's playbill is also one.

clue.text: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?

definitions.text: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?

parts.words: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?
parts.note: searched for food; and meals on wheels, the delivery service, is provided for elderly people

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'for aged': meals on wheels is a British service delivering hot meals to elderly people. The held text seems to repeat 'wheels'.
explanation.definitionFit: To search widely for food is to scavenge, and a food delivery service for elderly people is 'for the old'.

clue.text: A bit of leg gives nothing but youthful infatuation

parts.note: the calf is the back part of the lower leg
love is a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Showing a glimpse of leg brings out a teenager's crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives nothing but' looks like a phrase of denial; LOVE is the tennis word for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief, intense romantic crush felt by an adolescent is given this name.

clue.text: Enquiring how a monarch rules

definitions.meaning: putting a question
a monarch rules in the role of the crowned sovereign

explanation.definitionFit: Requesting information is putting a question, and a crowned ruler governs in the role of sovereign, split as two words.

clue.text: All that is left for housing development

definitions.meaning: everything a dead person leaves behind, their assets
a planned area of homes built together

explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's whole property and possessions are known by this word, as is a planned area of new homes.

clue.text: Accommodation for camping campanologists

parts.note: bell-ringers sleeping out under canvas would want shelters with a bell-like name and shape

explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers; a bell tent is a round tent with a single central pole, shaped like a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Conical, single-pole canvas shelters shaped like a bell suit bell-ringers on a camping trip.

clue.text: Cruel misappropriation of profit

indicators.note: funds misappropriated are diverted wrongly, so the letters of the word are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Ruthless embezzlement of a company's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misappropriation of' rearranges CRUEL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or gain, especially when seen as dishonest or sordid, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Smallest amount of stale crumble

indicators.note: to crumble is to fall to pieces, so the letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of old cake falls to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means the minimum, as in 'the very least you can do'.

clue.text: Organised vice Heath drove out

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, arranged afresh

parts.note: Ted Heath, British prime minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A political scandal: organised vice drove Prime Minister Heath from office.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was a Conservative British prime minister; 'Organised' rearranges VICE with TED.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from a property, forcing them out.

clue.text: Rude suggestion as to where Newport visitors should bathe

parts.note: the preposition naming a location, 'in'
Newport is the main town on the Isle of Wight, beside the Solent, the strait off southern England

explanation.surface: Advising tourists on the Isle of Wight where to swim could seem impertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight (whose county town is Newport) and mainland England, so visitors bathe 'in Solent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is disrespectful and cheeky, which is what rude means here.

clue.text: French preposition in oral test

indicators.note: the French word is placed inside the spoken exam

parts.note: de is French for of or from

explanation.surface: A French preposition comes up in a spoken examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral test' looks like the definition together; 'test' alone defines, ORAL holds DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial or painful experience tests endurance; medieval trial by ordeal was literally a test.
